issues.problem: Announced "three facts" but the third (kernel and image are subgroups) was only asserted "as these two facts show"; mild padding in the exp example.
issues.fix: Reworded to two facts plus a consequence; trimmed the "same structure in disguise" sentence.

issues.problem: The computation that kernels are normal skipped the step $\varphi(gng^{-1}) = \varphi(g)\varphi(n)\varphi(g)^{-1}$, so it read as $\varphi(gng^{-1}) = \varphi(g)\varphi(g)^{-1}$ with no justification.
issues.fix: Inserted the missing middle step.

issues.problem: Primitive-root statement omitted the kernel needed to apply the first isomorphism theorem; Galois statement said "themselves Galois" without saying over which field.
issues.fix: Stated the kernel $(p-1)\mathbb Z$ and "Galois over the base field".

issues.where: section/Using the first isomorphism theorem; example/A cyclic quotient by the centre; pitfall
issues.problem: Padding: circle-gluing remark, "Notice what this says", and a pitfall item (abelian quotient of a non-abelian group) that is not a mistake anyone makes.
issues.fix: Removed.

issues.where: intro; section/Examples, orbits and stabilisers; proof of Burnside
issues.problem: Hype and padding ("how groups are used in practice", "culminating", naming anecdote).
issues.fix: Trimmed.

issues.problem: The proof sketch said parts 2 and 3 follow from letting a Sylow subgroup act by conjugation on the Sylow subgroups. That action gives conjugacy and $n_p \equiv 1 \pmod p$, but not $n_p \mid m$, which needs the conjugation action of all of $G$ (stabiliser $N_G(P) \supseteq P$). The text also did not say clearly that parts 2 and 3 are stated without proof.
issues.fix: Said explicitly that parts 2 and 3 are stated without proof and corrected the sketch: $P$ acting gives conjugacy and $n_p \equiv 1$; $G$ acting gives $n_p \mid [G:P] = m$.

issues.problem: "$\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z$ ... has zero divisors otherwise" is false for $n = 1$ (the zero ring has no zero divisors).
issues.fix: Restricted to composite $n > 1$.

issues.where: section/Quotient rings; proof of the first isomorphism theorem for rings
issues.problem: The lesson relied on normal subgroups and the first isomorphism theorem for groups ([[group-homomorphisms]]), which is not a prerequisite of this concept (prerequisites: groups, congruences).
issues.fix: Made both arguments self-contained (direct well-definedness of addition; direct proof that the induced map is well defined and injective).

issues.problem: "Idempotents detect exactly how a ring splits as a product" is vague.
issues.fix: Replaced with the precise statement that a nontrivial idempotent gives a splitting into a product of two rings.

issues.problem: Padding and repetition (pitfall repeating the gallery; connection repeating the catalog link note).
issues.fix: Trimmed.

issues.problem: Key statement "$R/I$ is a field iff $I$ is maximal" was shown without the commutativity hypothesis; it fails for non-commutative rings (e.g. $M_2(\mathbb R)$ with $I = 0$: maximal, but the quotient is not a field).
issues.fix: Added "R commutative" to the key statement.

issues.problem: Uniqueness of splitting fields was stated loosely ("unique up to isomorphism") without saying the isomorphism fixes K, and without saying it is stated without proof; the definition of splitting field was informal ("the field generated by all the roots" presupposes an ambient field).
issues.fix: Gave the precise definition, stated uniqueness up to a K-isomorphism, and flagged it as a standard result used without proof.

issues.problem: $\varphi(n)$ used without saying it is Euler\'s function.
issues.fix: Named it and linked [[arithmetic-functions]].

issues.problem: Hype ("remarkably rigid invariant") and a wordy finite-field aside.
issues.fix: Tightened.

issues.problem: Historical aside and application list duplicated the connection block.
issues.fix: Removed.

issues.problem: The factorisation of $x^{p^n} - x$ into all monic irreducibles of degree dividing $n$ was asserted "with a little more work", with only one direction (each such $f$ divides) argued; the converse (every irreducible factor has degree dividing $n$) and the absence of repeated factors were missing, yet the Möbius formula and the example depend on the exact statement.
issues.fix: Added the two missing steps (root in the subfield plus tower law; distinct roots), so the statement is now proved.

issues.problem: "Primitive elements are not unique" is false for $q = 2$ and $q = 3$, where $\varphi(q-1) = 1$. The Frobenius pitfall was muddled: the field $\mathbb F_9$ has characteristic $3$, so the point is the exponent, not the characteristic.
issues.fix: Said "usually not unique" with an example; reworded the Frobenius pitfall in terms of the exponent.

issues.problem: BCH codes are not evaluation codes in the sense described; the note did not say what the root bound buys.
issues.fix: Restricted to Reed–Solomon codes and stated the distance bound it gives.

issues.problem: Wordy history.
issues.fix: Shortened.

issues.problem: "Changing the sign of $\sqrt 2$ throughout a true identity keeps it true" is not a justification (it is what is to be shown).
issues.fix: Replaced by the explicit product formula.

issues.problem: "Equality exactly when all $n$ roots of $m$ lie in $L$" silently uses separability (without it, $m$ can split over $L$ with fewer than $n$ distinct roots, e.g. inseparable extensions in characteristic $p$, where equality fails).
issues.fix: Made the use of distinct roots explicit in the statement and the proof.

issues.problem: The primitive element theorem and the characterisation of Galois extensions were stated only in their special forms ("every finite extension is simple"; "Galois iff splitting field of some polynomial"), which are false in general (e.g. $\mathbb F_p(t^{1/p})/\mathbb F_p(t)$ is a splitting field but not Galois; $\mathbb F_p(s,t)/\mathbb F_p(s^p,t^p)$ is not simple).
issues.fix: Stated the exact results (finite separable extensions are simple; Galois iff normal and separable iff splitting field of a separable polynomial) and then specialised them to the lesson's setting with the reason.

issues.problem: "Given Artin's lemma, part 3 follows and the rest is bookkeeping" overstates it (parts 1 and 4 need further arguments) and did not clearly say the theorem is stated without proof.
issues.fix: Said plainly that the theorem is stated without proof, kept Artin's lemma as the key step, and cited part 3 in the fixed-field recipe.

issues.problem: Irreducibility of $\Phi_7$ was quoted with no indication of why; the extension was not said to be Galois before $L^G = \mathbb Q$ was used; "$\eta_k$ depends only on $k$ modulo 7 up to sign" is garbled.
issues.fix: Added the standard reason (Eisenstein at 7 for $\Phi_7(x+1)$), noted the extension is Galois of degree 6, and stated $\eta_{-k} = \eta_k$ explicitly.

issues.problem: Non-solvability of $S_5$ was justified by listing its normal subgroups, which does not by itself rule out a chain with abelian quotients, and the simplicity of $A_5$ and Galois\'s theorem were used without saying they are stated without proof.
issues.fix: Flagged simplicity of $A_5$ and Galois\'s theorem as standard results stated without proof, and gave the short correct deduction: a chain for $A_5$ would need the non-abelian quotient $A_5/\{e\}$, and subgroups of solvable groups are solvable.

issues.where: example/A quintic that cannot be solved by radicals
issues.problem: The splitting field $L$ was never set up as a subfield of $\mathbb C$, although complex conjugation acting on it is essential; distinctness of the five roots was implicit.
issues.fix: Defined $L \subseteq \mathbb C$ and $G$ explicitly. Hypotheses now all visible: irreducible (Eisenstein at 2), prime degree 5, exactly two non-real roots.

issues.where: example/The splitting field of x^3 - 2; pitfall; connection
issues.problem: Repetition (pitfall restating part 2 of the theorem) and an over-long connection; "controlled by Frobenius elements" needs the unramified caveat.
issues.fix: Trimmed; added "for all but finitely many primes".

issues.problem: The radical-solvability criterion was stated with no characteristic hypothesis (it fails in characteristic p, e.g. for Artin–Schreier extensions); "Galois group of a field extension" should be of a Galois extension (otherwise it is only the automorphism group).
issues.fix: Added "in characteristic 0" to sum and key, and "Galois extension" to the sum.

issues.problem: The covering-space correspondence was stated for every space and all covering spaces; it needs connectedness and local conditions, and concerns connected (based) coverings.
issues.fix: Added the hypotheses and the normal-subgroup/deck-group analogue.

issues.problem: Lesson far over length; this example alone was over 500 words, with a long symmetric-function computation.
issues.fix: Kept the group, the quadratic subfield and the Gauss-sum remark; identified the cubic subfield in three sentences and moved the computation of the minimal polynomial of 2cos(2pi/7) to exercise 3 (still covered by the existing check).

issues.problem: Frobenius elements describe splitting only for unramified primes in Galois extensions.
issues.fix: Added both qualifiers.

issues.problem: "Countably infinite" and "pairwise disjoint" are not school vocabulary.
issues.fix: Glossed both in plain words.

issues.where: section/Rules that follow from the axioms
issues.problem: The derivation of $P(\varnothing) = 0$ was compressed to a phrase a 15-year-old cannot unpack, and the union bound was stated with no reason although the section says everything follows from the axioms.
issues.fix: Spelled out both in one or two sentences.

issues.problem: Mutual independence was defined with double subscripts $A_{i_1}, \dots, A_{i_k}$, heavy for a school-stage reader.
issues.fix: Defined it in words and wrote out the three-event case.

issues.problem: The variant with an ignorant host reused the letter H for a different event and was hard to parse.
issues.fix: Rewrote it with its own event E and the full Bayes computation in words.

issues.problem: The error bound $|p_n - 1/e| < 1/(n+1)!$ was asserted with no reason a school reader would know.
issues.fix: Gave the alternating-series reason in words.

issues.problem: Repetition of points already made in the examples; jargon ("uncountable") in the connection.
issues.fix: Trimmed and simplified.
